gates.premise_review_note: Flowchart drawn and one mismatch reported before initialization: the stack document and the motion research both recorded that the application could rotate an image from a script. Checked against the application's source - it cannot. Both documents corrected in their own commit before this track was created.
gates.code_review_note: Carried out in the session that owns the track after both review subagents stopped on a usage limit before executing anything. Two blockers found and fixed: a part reaching past the drawing assembled bytes from the wrong end of the buffer into colours the drawing never held, and an animation where every frame composited to nothing reported success over blank tagged frames. Every finding was reproduced by running it.
gates.security_review_note: Mandatory because the track adds scripts that read and write files. No external call, subprocess, network access or dynamic code loading anywhere in the shipped extension, which is what needing no permission dialog rests on. Only main.lua ships; tools and tests are never packaged. Committed binaries are small: the sample 1635 bytes, all twenty reference frames 6509 bytes. The automated checks were untouched, so the three deferred rows keep their severity. Eight crafted rigs were all refused with a message naming the part.
gates.mutation_testing_note: Sixteen deliberate breaks, one at a time. Fifteen caught. The survivor was the sign of the sideways term in the forward kinematics, which survived because every placement check had the child directly above or below its parent; closed with two cases for a part off to the side.
gates.backlog_reconciliation_note: Five rows existed and none had an issue on the remote, although the rule has required both since the remote arrived. All are open now and linked both ways. Reconciliation also raised a sixth: nothing builds the distribution archive, so the security review's claim about what ships is true of the manifest and enforced by nothing.
